title: Crispy Honey Chili Sausage
subtitle: A dozen eggs and cheese baked between two layers of slider rolls.
description: Eggs baked on a sheet pan, cut into squares, and layered on toasted buns with sausage and cheese. Ten sandwiches without flipping eggs one at a time.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Crispy Honey Chili Sausage in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Sausage. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 350°F. Slice the connected roll block horizontally into tops and bottoms without separating individual rolls. Allow 10–15 minutes for mise en place before heat goes on. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Bake the egg sheet
steps.instruction: Whisk eggs with milk, salt, and pepper. Pour into a parchment-lined quarter sheet pan to roughly slider dimensions. Bake until just set—don't overbake or eggs turn rubbery.

steps.title: Trim and assemble
steps.instruction: Trim egg sheet to fit the roll block. Place bottom halves on a lined sheet pan, add sausage, egg sheet, cheese, and top halves. Press gently to align seams.

steps.title: Final bake
steps.instruction: Brush tops with melted butter and optional everything seasoning. Bake until cheese melts and tops turn lightly golden. Bake until the center reaches a safe internal temp (165°F) and edges look set — use a thermometer at the thickest point. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Cut and serve
steps.instruction: Rest 5 minutes, then cut along roll seams with a sharp knife. Serve warm from the pan or transfer to a hotel pan for the line. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Measure the roll block before baking the egg sheet—trim once, not twice, for clean sandwich edges.
Use parchment to lift the egg sheet out of the quarter pan for easier trimming and placement.
Cut seams with a long serrated knife in one pass per row to avoid squashing the stacks.
cleanupNotes: Discard parchment with baked-on egg residue instead of scraping—saves time on busy mornings.
Wipe the sheet pan while warm with a damp towel before butter glaze hardens on the rim.
leftovers: Wrap sandwiches individually in foil and reheat at 325°F for 10 minutes until cheese remelts.
Split leftovers and griddle cut-side down for a crisp second-day version with fresh hot sauce.
